title: Differential shredding lifecycle controller for request artifacts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a unified lifecycle controller for request artifacts (prompts, responses, request logs, and derived metrics) that supports differential shredding, residency-aware retention, and forensics-ready evidence exports. The controller should let tenants declare per-route retention policies, apply safe transformations (shredding/hash-derivation) at configurable retention boundaries, and produce attestable evidence bundles for audits. This work couples runtime eviction hooks with a policy engine and a compact evidence packaging pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route policy table is queryable via config API and supports: keep_seconds, shred_after_seconds, residency_region, retention_profile
When shred_after_seconds is reached, PII fields in prompts/responses can be replaced by deterministic hash+salt and original text evicted while maintaining proof-of-eviction metadata
Evidence export job can assemble attestable bundle (manifest, hashes, signed timestamps) for a tenant and time window
End-to-end automated test exercising retention lifecycle for prompts -> shred -> archive -> evidence export
No regression in tail-latency for hot paths under typical traffic (<=+3% p95 tokens latency) with feature flag off-by-default
implementation_notes: Policy datastore: extend existing runtime-config service with policy versioning and per-route lookup cache (LRU with 60s TTL)
Shredding primitive: implement deterministic HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-specific salt stored in KMS; return canonical placeholder format: <SHRED:v1:hk>
Eviction flow: hook into KV cache eviction and disk-backed request-store; eviction should emit provenance record (artifact id, orig-length, hash, shred_version)
Evidence bundle: use compressed tar with JSON manifest, signature via platform signing key, and include provenance chain for each artifact
Feature flags: runtime.shredding.enable and runtime.shredding.mode (GRACEFUL|FORCE) to allow controlled rollout
Backward compatibility: provide shim for existing retention TTLs; map existing ttl -> shred_after unless tenant opts out
risks_and_tradeoffs: Deterministic hashing preserves ability to correlate repeated PII across events which may be undesirable for some customers; provide opt-out to use one-way salted hash with per-eviction random nonce (breaks cross-event correlation)
Shredding in hot path can add CPU; mitigate via batching background workers and using async eviction where possible
Evidence bundle size can grow rapidly for high-throughput tenants; include sampled export mode and manifest-only exports for low-cost audits
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement controller and unit tests behind feature flag; internal e2e using synthetic tenant
Phase 2 (canary): enable for small set of low-throughput tenants with retention profiles, monitor latency and storage churn
Phase 3 (gradual): add residency enforcement and evidence-export job; enable opt-in in Console UI
Phase 4 (GA): document API, run security review, and flip feature flag for orgs that accept shredding semantics
tests: unit: policy parser and conflict resolution tests
integration: end-to-end retention lifecycle (ingest -> shred -> export) using test harness
load: simulate 10k rps with mixed routes and assert latency/regression limits
security: KMS integration tests for salt retrieval and rotation
forensics: validate manifest signatures verify and provenance chain reconstruction
